title: Why We Migrated Our Distributed Storage Engine from Go to Rust
summary: An architectural deep dive into the performance bottlenecks encountered when scaling a high-throughput key-value store in Go. The article analyzes how stop-the-world garbage collection pauses impacted p99 tail latency and details the memory safety, concurrency primitives, and zero-cost abstractions leveraged during the Rust rewrite to achieve a 40% reduction in resource allocation.

title: Reverse Engineering Proprietary Firmware via Side-Channel Voltage Analysis
summary: A technical breakdown detailing the extraction of cryptographic keys from an isolated microcontroller using differential power analysis and fault injection. The post outlines the custom hardware setup utilizing a low-cost oscilloscope, open-source signal processing pipelines, and mitigations for hardware designers against physical tampering.

title: Determining Optical Flow in Embedded Vision Systems Using Sparse Matrices
summary: A mathematical formulation and C23 implementation for computing real-time motion vectors on resource-constrained microcontrollers. By replacing dense matrix operations with block-sparse approximations, the proposed algorithm achieves a 120 Hz frame rate on ARM Cortex-M microcontrollers without dedicated hardware acceleration.

title: Post-Mortem: A 4-Hour Global Outage Triggered by BGP Route Flapping
summary: An incident analysis of a cascading network failure across multi-region edge locations. The report investigates how a misconfigured autonomous system number (ASN) aggregation rule interacted with downstream route reflectors, causing control plane saturation and subsequent DNS resolution failures across all major points of presence.

title: Formal Verification of a Concurrent Lock-Free Queue in TLA+
summary: An exploration of applying formal methods to concurrent data structure design. The author presents a complete TLA+ specification for a multi-producer, multi-consumer queue, proving the absence of deadlocks, race conditions, and ABA problems before generating verified C code using explicit model checking.

title: Implementing Quantized LLM Inference Engines directly in WebAssembly
summary: A practical exploration of executing 4-bit quantized transformer models within the browser without WebGPU dependencies. The write-up highlights SIMD optimizations, custom WebAssembly linear algebra kernels, and memory mapping techniques required to maintain sub-second token generation rates on mobile client devices.

title: Query Optimization Strategies for Multi-Tenant Time-Series Databases
summary: A study on partition indexing, LSM-tree compaction heuristics, and compression algorithms optimized for high-cardinality telemetry data. The discussion compares columnar storage efficiency, delta-of-delta encoding, and segment skip-indexes under heavy concurrent write loads.

title: Zero-Knowledge Proofs in Practice: Building an Anonymous Credential System
summary: A step-by-step implementation guide for an identity verification system based on zk-SNARKs. It details the construction of arithmetic circuits using Circom, setup of trusted setups, and implementation of client-side proof generation to enable authentication without disclosing personally identifiable information.

title: The Evolution of Garbage Collection Algorithms in Modern Runtimes
summary: A comparative survey tracing the design trade-offs between generational mark-compact collectors, concurrent tri-color marking, and region-based memory management. The paper evaluates throughput, pause-time guarantees, and cache locality metrics across Java's ZGC, Go's concurrent collector, and V8's Orinoco.

title: Compiling Subsets of Python to eBPF Bytecode for Kernel Observability
summary: An introduction to a custom compiler toolchain designed to translate a restricted subset of Python syntax directly into Extended Berkeley Packet Filter (eBPF) bytecode. The post discusses AST parsing, register allocation within kernel verifier constraints, and real-time network packet filtering applications.
